title: AI agents now decide where tech is bought, so our store must be agent-ready
summary: Counterpoint: Q3 PC shipments fell 21%, Q4 seen down 27%, record price inflation on memory costs. NIQ: 55% use AI in discovery. Walmart opened to outside AI agents; Google launched Universal Cart; Amex built agent-purchase verification; Best Buy joined TikTok Shop.

points.headline: Retailers, Google, Meta and Amex are setting the rules for AI buying agents
points.detail: Walmart lets outside agents buy under new terms while Amazon blocks them; Google opened Universal Cart; Amex launched agent-purchase verification. We should decide how agents read and buy from our store.

points.headline: PC demand is falling just as memory costs push prices up
points.detail: Shipments fell 21% in Q3 with Q4 forecast down 27%, while AI data center demand keeps memory undersupplied and drives record PC price inflation. We should plan pricing, promotions and inventory for thin margins.

points.headline: AI is now a mainstream way shoppers discover products
points.detail: NIQ finds 55% of consumers use AI in product discovery; Gartner says 34% of US consumers would use GenAI for holiday gift ideas. Our product content and feeds must work in AI tools, not only search.

points.headline: Electronics retailers are adding channels for the holiday peak
points.detail: Best Buy joined TikTok Shop for its biggest holiday season, and Adobe forecasts US online holiday sales of $275.1B. We should test our presence on new channels.
